items.stem: What do the elders pray for?
options: A gentle, tearless doom, and entry without pain
A victory already won against a neighbouring army
Rain for the fields around the sacred grove
A sudden end already planned for Creon and his men

items.stem: How do the elders now describe Oedipus' life?
options: Wrongfully oppressed
Lucky in every season
Royal and still in power
Wicked by his own design

items.stem: Complete the line: “Hear, Goddess dread, _____!”
options: merciful
earthly
invisible
silent

items.stem: Complete the line: “Monarch of the regions _____,”
options: bright
crowded
distant
drear

items.stem: What does “Stygian” refer to?
options: The underworld, named from the river Styx
A mountain standing over the sacred grove
A city already named in the earlier odes
A temple the chorus has already promised to build

items.stem: Why do the elders ask that the stranger enter without pain?
options: They petition the powers below to speed him gently and spare him suffering
They want him to stay in the grove and refuse any summons at all this hour
They hope the daughters will lead him back to a neighbouring city now
They mean to finish a sacrifice before the prince can return to them

items.stem: What is the tone of the prayer?
options: Gentle and reverent
Angry and accusing
Comic and light-hearted
Boastful and triumphant

items.stem: How have the elders changed since the Parodos?
options: From driving him away to praying for him
From praise of him to open blame of the king
They have not changed in any important way
From fear of the grove to anger at Theseus

items.stem: Which underworld king do the elders call by name in this ode?
options: Aidoneus
King Creon
King Theseus
Lord Apollo

items.stem: Complete the line: “Queen _____, and thou fell”
options: Athenian
mortal
gentle
infernal

items.stem: Complete the line: “Gnarling in thy _____ lair”
options: narrow
sunlit
cavernous
crowded

items.stem: What do the elders ask the watch-dog of the gates to do?
options: Let him go scathless to the fields below
Bar the gate and keep the stranger out forever
Hunt the daughters back from the grove at once
Devour every comer who has already reached the plain

items.stem: Who, according to the ode, gives the order that the stranger be let go?
options: The watch-dog's master, called the son of earth and the deep underworld
The chorus itself, speaking in the name of the Athenian king this hour
Antigone, who has already asked the hound to stand aside at the gate
Creon, who has already claimed the right to take the stranger home

items.stem: Which literary element is at work when the prayer names Aidoneus, the Stygian plain, and the watch-dog of the gates?
options: Allusion
Comic mode
Satiric mode
Ironic mode

items.stem: What do the elders ask Justice to do?
options: Bless Oedipus now, after a life they call wrongful oppression
Condemn him again for deeds already judged in a neighbouring city
Send him back at once to finish a war already begun in the field
Silence the watch-dog before the daughters can speak at all

items.stem: Complete the line: “The son of earth and _____;”
options: Olympus
Colonus
Thebes
Tartarus

items.stem: Complete the line: “In his den the _____ keep,”
options: stranger
monster
herald
elder

items.stem: Who, according to the Chorus, is the watch-dog's master in this ode?
options: The underworld king who orders the hound to let the stranger go
Theseus, who has already claimed the grove as his own court now
The chorus leader, who now speaks as if he ruled the world of the dead
Creon, who has already demanded that the stranger be returned at once

items.stem: Why do the elders ask that the stranger go unharmed to the fields below?
options: They ask that he be allowed to enter the underworld unharmed
They want the hound to drive him back into the grove at once
They have already seen him refused and sent away empty-handed
They mean to hide the place of rest from every later visitor

items.stem: Which literary element names the feeling of a prayer that asks for a gentle, tearless doom and a blessing by Justice?
options: Tone
Plot
Comedy
Satire

items.stem: Complete the line: “The all-shrouding _____ plain.”
options: Athenian
Theban
Stygian
Argive

items.stem: Complete the line: “Giver of _____ sleep.”
options: gentle
sudden
eternal
earthly

items.stem: How does calling Oedipus's life wrongful oppression prepare the prayer that Justice bless him now?
options: It first revises the verdict on his suffering, then asks that blessing follow
It accuses him again, so that Justice will refuse any blessing at all now
It claims he has already been blessed, and that the prayer is unnecessary now
It tells the daughters to take him home before any blessing can be asked

items.stem: How does the watch-dog image work in the prayer, if the same song also asks that the stranger go unharmed?
options: The fierce guardian is asked, under its master's order, to make an exception of this stranger
The hound is praised for already having barred every path to the stranger this day
The image is comic, and it asks the audience to laugh at the underworld outright
The image warns Theseus to hunt the stranger out of the grove at once today

items.stem: What is the effect of closing the ode by naming a giver of last rest?
options: It names the underworld power as the one who grants a last rest
It tells us that the stranger has already been laid to rest before the song began
It names that power as a civic official already seated in the Athenian council
It claims to reveal a hidden grave that no one in the city may later name

items.stem: Which reading of the ode best holds its mythic names and its moral petition together?
options: A religious song asking the powers below to receive, without pain, a man they now call wronged
A war song that asks Aidoneus to destroy a neighbouring city for Athens this day
A comic interlude that mocks the stranger for having entered the sacred grove
A report that already confirms how the end will later be told on the stage
